label: thm:mainint
title: Theorem
body_md:
\label{thm:mainint}
Let $\pi_d: \overline{J}^d_C \to B$ and $\pi^\vee: \overline{J}_C^\vee \to B$ be as in Sections \ref{sec:2.1} and \ref{sec:2.2}.
\begin{enumerate}
\item[(i)] (Fourier-stability) For integers $k, l$, the perverse truncation
\[
{\mathfrak{F}}^d_l: {^{\mathfrak{p}}}\tau_{\leq k + \dim B}(\pi_*^\vee{\mathbb{Q}}_{\overline{J}_C^\vee}) \to \pi_{d*}{\mathbb{Q}}_{\overline{J}^d_C}[2l - 2g]
\]
is zero if $l < 2g - k$, and factors through
\[
{\mathfrak{F}}^d_l: {^{\mathfrak{p}}}\tau_{\leq k + \dim B}(\pi_*^\vee{\mathbb{Q}}_{\overline{J}_C^\vee}) \to {^{\mathfrak{p}}}\tau_{\leq l + \dim B}(\pi_{d*}{\mathbb{Q}}_{\overline{J}^d_C})[2l - 2g]
\]
if $l \geq 2g - k$. Similarly, the perverse truncation
\[
({\mathfrak{F}}^d)^{-1}_l: {^{\mathfrak{p}}}\tau_{\leq k + \dim B}(\pi_{d*}{\mathbb{Q}}_{\overline{J}_C^d}) \to \pi_*^\vee{\mathbb{Q}}_{\overline{J}^\vee_C}[2l - 2g]
\]
is zero if $l < 2g - k$, and factors through
\[
({\mathfrak{F}}^d)^{-1}_l: {^{\mathfrak{p}}}\tau_{\leq k + \dim B}(\pi_{d*}{\mathbb{Q}}_{\overline{J}_C^d}) \to {^{\mathfrak{p}}}\tau_{\leq l + \dim B}(\pi_*^\vee{\mathbb{Q}}_{\overline{J}^\vee_C})[2l - 2g]
\]
if $l \geq 2g - k$. For $0 \leq k \leq 2g$, ${\mathfrak{F}}^d_k$ and $({\mathfrak{F}}^d)^{-1}_{2g - k}$ induce mutually inverse isomorphisms
\begin{equation} \label{eq:isomH}
{\mathcal H}^\vee_{(2g - k)}[2g - 2k] \xrightleftharpoons[\overline{({\mathfrak{F}}^d)_{2g - k}^{-1}}]{\overline{{\mathfrak{F}}^d_k}} {\mathcal H}^d_{(k)}.
\end{equation}

\item[(ii)] (Multiplicativity for $*_{\mathrm{red}}$) For integers $k, l$, the perverse truncation
\[
*_{\mathrm{red}}: {^{\mathfrak{p}}}\tau_{\leq k + \dim B}(\pi_*^\vee{\mathbb{Q}}_{\overline{J}_C^\vee})  \otimes {^{\mathfrak{p}}}\tau_{\leq l + \dim B}(\pi_*^\vee{\mathbb{Q}}_{\overline{J}_C^\vee}) \to \pi_*^\vee{\mathbb{Q}}_{\overline{J}_C^\vee}[-2g],
\]
of the reduced convolution product in \eqref{eq:trunconv} factors through
\[
*_{\mathrm{red}}: {^{\mathfrak{p}}}\tau_{\leq k + \dim B}(\pi_*^\vee{\mathbb{Q}}_{\overline{J}_C^\vee})  \otimes {^{\mathfrak{p}}}\tau_{\leq l + \dim B}(\pi_*^\vee{\mathbb{Q}}_{\overline{J}_C^\vee}) \to {^{\mathfrak{p}}}\tau_{\leq k + l -2g + \dim B}(\pi_*^\vee{\mathbb{Q}}_{\overline{J}_C^\vee})[-2g],
\]
In particular, the reduced convolution product descends to a collection of morphisms
\begin{equation} \label{eq:trunconvbarkl}
\overline{*}_{\mathrm{red}}: {\mathcal H}^\vee_{(k)} \otimes {\mathcal H}^\vee_{(l)} \to {\mathcal H}^\vee_{(k + l - 2g)}[-2g].
\end{equation}

\item[(iii)] (Degree-independence) The graded ring object ${\mathcal H}^d \in D^b_c(B)$ in \eqref{eq:defCH} is completely determined by the morphisms $\overline{*}_{\mathrm{red}}$. In particular, for integers $d, d'$, there is an isomorphism
\[
{\mathcal H}^d \simeq {\mathcal H}^{d'} \in D^b_c(B)
\]
of graded ring objects.
\end{enumerate}

label: eq:fstable
title: Proof
body_md:
Essentially all three parts are consequences of the Fourier vanishing. We begin with part (i). In view of the realization Theorem \ref{thm:realize}, for the first statement of (i) it suffices to show
\begin{gather}
{\mathfrak{F}}^d_l \circ {\mathfrak{p}}^\vee_{\leq k} = 0, \quad l < 2g - k, \label{eq:fstable} \\
{\mathfrak{q}}^d_{\geq l + 1} \circ {\mathfrak{F}}^d_l = 0, \label{eq:fstable2}
\end{gather}
where ${\mathfrak{q}}^d_{\geq l + 1}$ is defined in \eqref{eq:defq}. Expanding the left-hand side of both equations
\begin{gather*}
{\mathfrak{F}}^d_l \circ {\mathfrak{p}}^\vee_{\leq k} = \sum_{i \leq k} {\mathfrak{F}}^d_l \circ ({\mathfrak{F}}^d)^{-1}_i \circ {\mathfrak{F}}^d_{2g - i}, \\
{\mathfrak{q}}^d_{\geq l + 1} \circ {\mathfrak{F}}^d_l = \sum_{i \geq l + 1} {\mathfrak{F}}^d_i \circ ({\mathfrak{F}}^d)^{-1}_{2g - i} \circ {\mathfrak{F}}^d_l,
\end{gather*}
we see that \eqref{eq:fstable} (resp.~\eqref{eq:fstable2}) follows directly from (FV2) (resp.~(FV1)). The second statement of (i) is parallel.

To prove \eqref{eq:isomH} we first observe that
\[
({\mathfrak{F}}^d)^{-1}_{2g - k} \circ {\mathfrak{p}}_{\leq k - 1}^d = 0;
\]
hence $({\mathfrak{F}}^d)^{-1}_{2g - k}$ descends to a well-defined morphism
\[
\overline{({\mathfrak{F}}^d)^{-1}_{2g - k}}: {\mathcal H}^d_{(k)} \to {\mathcal H}^\vee_{(2g - k)}[2g - 2k].
\]
Similarly, ${\mathfrak{F}}^d_k$ descends to a well-defined morphism
\[
\overline{{\mathfrak{F}}^d_k}: {\mathcal H}^\vee_{(2g - k)}[2g - 2k] \to {\mathcal H}^d_{(k)}.
\]
To show that they are inverse to each other, we consider the identities
\begin{align}
{\mathfrak{p}}_{\leq k}^d & = {\mathfrak{F}}^d \circ ({\mathfrak{F}}^d)^{-1} \circ {\mathfrak{p}}_{\leq k}^d = \sum_{i \geq 2g - k} {\mathfrak{F}}^d_{2g - i} \circ ({\mathfrak{F}}^d)^{-1}_i \circ {\mathfrak{p}}_{\leq k}^d \nonumber \\
& = {\mathfrak{F}}^d_k \circ ({\mathfrak{F}}^d)^{-1}_{2g - k} \circ {\mathfrak{p}}_{\leq k}^d + \sum_{i > 2g - k} {\mathfrak{F}}^d_{2g - i} \circ ({\mathfrak{F}}^d)^{-1}_i \circ {\mathfrak{p}}_{\leq k}^d \label{eq:expand}
\end{align}
where the second identity holds both by (FV1) and for dimension reasons. Now the condition~$i > 2g - k$
translates to $2g - i < k$, which implies that the entire second term in \eqref{eq:expand} factors through
\[
{^{\mathfrak{p}}}\tau_{\leq k + \dim B}(\pi_{d*}{\mathbb{Q}}_{\overline{J}_C^d}) \to {^{\mathfrak{p}}}\tau_{\leq k - 1 + \dim B}(\pi_{d*}{\mathbb{Q}}_{\overline{J}_C^d}).
\]
Therefore we have
\[
\mathrm{id} = \overline{{\mathfrak{F}}^d_k} \circ \overline{({\mathfrak{F}}^d)^{-1}_{2g - k}}: {\mathcal H}^d_{(k)} \to {\mathcal H}^d_{(k)}.
\]
The other direction is parallel. This proves (i).

For (ii) we consider via \eqref{eq:commconv} the identity
\[
*^d = ({\mathfrak{F}}^d)^{-1} \circ \cup \circ ({\mathfrak{F}}^d \otimes {\mathfrak{F}}^d).
\]
For dimension reasons we then have
\begin{equation} \label{eq:convexpand}
*_{\mathrm{red}} = \sum_i\sum_j({\mathfrak{F}}^d)^{-1}_{2g - i - j} \circ \cup \circ ({\mathfrak{F}}^d_i \otimes {\mathfrak{F}}^d_j).
\end{equation}
Again, in view of the realization Theorem \ref{thm:realize}, to prove (ii) it suffices to show
\[
{\mathfrak{q}}^\vee_{\geq k + l + 1 - 2g} \circ *_{\mathrm{red}} \circ ({\mathfrak{p}}^\vee_{\leq k} \otimes {\mathfrak{p}}^\vee_{\leq l}) = 0
\]
where ${\mathfrak{q}}^\vee_{\geq k + l + 1 - 2g}$ is defined in \eqref{eq:defq2}. We expand $*_{\mathrm{red}}$ using \eqref{eq:convexpand}, and find
\begin{align*}
& {\mathfrak{q}}^\vee_{\geq k + l + 1 - 2g} \circ *_{\mathrm{red}} \circ ({\mathfrak{p}}^\vee_{\leq k} \otimes {\mathfrak{p}}^\vee_{\leq l}) \\
{}= & \sum_i\sum_j {\mathfrak{q}}^\vee_{\geq k + l + 1 - 2g} \circ ({\mathfrak{F}}^d)^{-1}_{2g - i - j} \circ \cup \circ \left(({\mathfrak{F}}^d_i \circ {\mathfrak{p}}^\vee_{\leq k}) \otimes ({\mathfrak{F}}^d_j \circ {\mathfrak{p}}^\vee_{\leq l})\right) \\
{}= & \sum_{i \geq 2g - k}\sum_{j \geq 2g - l} {\mathfrak{q}}^\vee_{\geq k + l + 1 - 2g} \circ ({\mathfrak{F}}^d)^{-1}_{2g - i - j} \circ \cup \circ \left(({\mathfrak{F}}^d_i \circ {\mathfrak{p}}^\vee_{\leq k}) \otimes ({\mathfrak{F}}^d_j \circ {\mathfrak{p}}^\vee_{\leq l})\right)
\end{align*}
where the second identity uses (FV2). This time the conditions $i \geq 2g - k$ and $j \geq 2g - l$ translate~to
\[
2g - i - j \leq k + l - 2g.
\]
But then we have
\[
{\mathfrak{q}}^\vee_{\geq k + l + 1 - 2g} \circ ({\mathfrak{F}}^d)^{-1}_{2g - i - j} = 0
\]
for such $i, j, k, l$ by (FV2). This proves (ii).

For (iii) we consider the following diagram
\begin{equation} \label{eq:diagram}
\begin{tikzcd}
{\mathcal H}^\vee_{(2g - k)}[2g - 2k] \otimes {\mathcal H}^\vee_{(2g - l)}[2g - 2l] \arrow[r, "\overline{*}_{\mathrm{red}}"] \arrow[d, shift left=1pt, harpoon, "\overline{{\mathfrak{F}}^d_k} \otimes \overline{{\mathfrak{F}}^d_l}"] & {\mathcal H}^\vee_{(2g - k - l)}[2g - 2k - 2l] \arrow[d, shift left=1pt, harpoon, "\overline{{\mathfrak{F}}^d_{k + l}}"] \\
{\mathcal H}^d_{(k)} \otimes {\mathcal H}^d_{(l)} \arrow[r, "\overline{\cup}"] \arrow[u, shift left=1pt, harpoon, "\overline{({\mathfrak{F}}^d)_{2g - k}^{-1}} \otimes \overline{({\mathfrak{F}}^d)_{2g - l}^{-1}}"] & {\mathcal H}^d_{(k + l)}, \arrow[u, shift left=1pt, harpoon, "\overline{({\mathfrak{F}}^d)_{2g - k - l}^{-1}}"]
\end{tikzcd}
\end{equation}
where the top and bottom rows are given by \eqref{eq:trunconvbarkl} and \eqref{eq:cupbarkl}, respectively, and the vertical arrows are isomorphisms by \eqref{eq:isomH}. We claim that the diagram commutes. Indeed, 
decomposing
\[
*^d = \sum_{c \geq g} *^d_c, \quad *^d_c: \pi^\vee_{*}{\mathbb{Q}}_{J^\vee_C} \otimes \pi^\vee_{*}{\mathbb{Q}}_{J^\vee_C} \to \pi^\vee_{*}{\mathbb{Q}}_{J^\vee_C}[{2c - 4g}]
\]
according to the codimension, we have $*^d_g = *_{\mathrm{red}}$. There are identities
\begin{align}
\cup \circ ({\mathfrak{p}}^d_{\leq k} \otimes {\mathfrak{p}}^d_{\leq l}) & = {\mathfrak{F}}^d \circ *^d \circ \left((({\mathfrak{F}}^d)^{-1} \circ {\mathfrak{p}}^d_{\leq k}) \otimes (({\mathfrak{F}}^d)^{-1} \circ {\mathfrak{p}}^d_{\leq l})\right) \nonumber\\
& = \sum_{c \geq g}\sum_{i \geq 2g - k}\sum_{j \geq 2g - l} {\mathfrak{F}}^d_{5g - i - j - c} \circ *^d_c \circ \left((({\mathfrak{F}}^d)^{-1}_i \circ {\mathfrak{p}}^d_{\leq k}) \otimes (({\mathfrak{F}}^d)^{-1}_j \circ {\mathfrak{p}}^d_{\leq l})\right) \label{eq:expandcommute}
\end{align}
where the second identity uses both (FV1) and dimension constraints. We observe that \eqref{eq:expandcommute} contains the term
\[
{\mathfrak{F}}^d_{k + l} \circ *_{\mathrm{red}} \circ \left((({\mathfrak{F}}^d)_{2g - k}^{-1} \circ {\mathfrak{p}}^d_{\leq k}) \otimes (({\mathfrak{F}}^d)_{2g - l}^{-1} \circ {\mathfrak{p}}^d_{\leq l})\right)
\]
and all the other terms satisfy
\[
5g - i - j - c < k + l.
\]
By (i), this means that all the other terms in \eqref{eq:expandcommute} factor through
\[
{^{\mathfrak{p}}}\tau_{\leq k + \dim B}(\pi_{d*}{\mathbb{Q}}_{\overline{J}_C^d}) \otimes {^{\mathfrak{p}}}\tau_{\leq l + \dim B}(\pi_{d*}{\mathbb{Q}}_{\overline{J}_C^d}) \to {^{\mathfrak{p}}}\tau_{\leq k + l - 1 + \dim B}(\pi_{d*}{\mathbb{Q}}_{\overline{J}_C^d})
\]
and hence descend to zero. This shows the commutativity of the diagram \eqref{eq:diagram}.

Finally, for any integer $d$, we conclude from (i) that there are mutually inverse graded isomorphisms
\begin{equation}\label{H_tilde}
\widetilde{{\mathcal H}}^\vee:=\bigoplus_{k = 0}^{2g}{\mathcal H}^\vee_{(2g - k)}[2g - 2k] \xrightleftharpoons[\oplus \overline{({\mathfrak{F}}^d)_{2g - k}^{-1}}]{\oplus \overline{{\mathfrak{F}}^d_k}} \bigoplus_{k = 0}^{2g}{\mathcal H}^d_{(k)} = {\mathcal H}^d.
\end{equation}
Moreover, by the commutative diagram \eqref{eq:diagram}, the above isomorphisms are compatible with the reduced convolution product $\overline{*}_{\mathrm{red}}$ on the left-hand side, and the cup-product $\overline{\cup}$ on the right-hand side. This proves (iii) since by Proposition \ref{prop:trunC}, the product $\overline{*}_{\mathrm{red}}$ on the left-hand side is independent of $d$. The proof of Theorem \ref{thm:mainint} is now complete.

label: thm:DAF
title: Theorem
body_md:
\label{thm:DAF}
Let $(M,B,M^\vee,{\mathcal P}, {\mathcal K})$ be a dualizable abelian fibration satisfying both \textup{(FV1)} and \textup{(FV2)}. Then the graded ring object ${\mathcal H}_M \in D^b_c(B)$ is completely determined by the reduced convolution class ${\mathfrak{C}}_{\mathrm{red}}$ in \eqref{conv_cycle}. In particular, given two dualizable abelian fibrations
\[
(M, B, M^\vee, {\mathcal P}, {\mathcal K}), \quad (M', B, M^\vee, {\mathcal P}', {\mathcal K}')
\]
satisfying \textup{(FV1)} and \textup{(FV2)}, we have two convolution classes
\[
{\mathfrak{C}} , {\mathfrak{C}}' \in \mathrm{CH}_{\leq 2g + \dim B}(M^\vee \times_B M^\vee \times_B M^\vee )\]
induced by ${\mathcal K}, {\mathcal K}'$ respectively. If we have a match for the reduced parts
\begin{equation*}\label{reduced_eq}
{\mathfrak{C}}_{\mathrm{red}} = {\mathfrak{C}}'_{\mathrm{red}} \in \mathrm{CH}_{2g+\dim B}(M^\vee \times_B M^\vee \times_B M^\vee ),
\end{equation*}
then there is an isomorphism
\[
{\mathcal H}_M \simeq {\mathcal H}_{M'} \in D^b_c(B)
\]
of graded ring objects.

title: Proof
body_md:
The proof is essentially identical to the one given for compactified Jacobians associated with integral curves in Section \ref{sec:2}. For a dualizable abelian fibration
    \[
    (M, B, M^\vee, {\mathcal P}, {\mathcal K}),
    \]
    we show that the graded ring object ${\mathcal H}_M$ is isomorphic via the Fourier transform to $\widetilde{{\mathcal H}}_{M^\vee}$ endowed with the convolution product induced by ${\mathfrak{C}}_{\mathrm{red}}$, as in (\ref{H_tilde}). The proof of Theorem \ref{thm:mainint} works \emph{verbatim}, since the only geometric inputs required are 
    \begin{enumerate}
        \item[(i)] the dimension bound for the support of the convolution kernel ${\mathcal K}$,
        \item[(ii)] the Fourier vanishing, and
        \item[(iii)] the full support property of $\pi, \pi^\vee$,
    \end{enumerate}
    all of which remain valid in the general setting. The rest of the argument is entirely formal.

only relies on the reduced convolution class ${\mathfrak{C}}_{\mathrm{red}}$ on $M^\vee\times_BM^\vee\times_B M^\vee$. As in Remark \ref{rem:chow}, the parallel statements at the Chow level is conditional on certain Bloch--Beilinson type motivic conjectures.

is of codimension $g$. Moreover, the Zariski closure

\]
is the only codimension $g$ irreducible component of $\mathrm{Supp}({\mathcal K})$; in particular, the codimension $g$ support of ${\mathcal K}$ is independent of the stability condition $\phi$.

title: Proof
body_md:
The proof is parallel to that of \cite[Proposition 3.2]{MSY}; the arguments there need to be generalized from integral curves to reduced curves, and this was already worked through in~\cite{MRV2} (in order to establish Theorem \ref{thm:FM_P}). For the reader's convenience, in the following, we explain in more detail that the $\delta$-regularity assumption not only guarantees that the support of ${\mathcal K}$ is of codimension $g$ as in \cite[Proposition 3.2]{MSY}, but also determines the support completely as stated here in the proposition.

We consider 
\[
{\mathcal K}_3: = p_{123 *}\left( p_{14}^* {\mathcal P} \otimes p_{24}^*{\mathcal P} \otimes p_{34}^*{\mathcal P}\right) \in D^b\mathrm{Coh}(\overline{J}_C^{\phi'} \times_B \overline{J}_C^{\phi'}\times_B \overline{J}_C^{\phi'})
\]
where the $p_{ijk}, p_{ij}$ are the natural projections from $\overline{J}_C^{\phi'} \times_B \overline{J}_C^{\phi'}\times_B \overline{J}_C^{\phi'} \times_B \overline{J}_C^\phi$. The convolution kernel (\ref{convolution11}) is governed by ${\mathcal K}_3$; it suffices to show that the restriction of ${\mathcal K}_3$ over $B\setminus B^\circ$ has codimension $>g$.

We consider $b\in B\setminus B^\circ$ (in particular, $\delta(b) >0$), and a point
\[
(F_1,F_2,F_3) \in Z_b:= \mathrm{Supp}({\mathcal K}_3) \cap (\overline{J}_{C_b}^{\phi'_b} )^{\times 3}. 
\]
By an identical argument as in the proof of \cite[Proposition 3.2]{MSY}, we have
\begin{equation}\label{smooth_id}
\bigotimes_{i=1}^3 ({F_i}|_{C^{\mathrm{reg}}_b} ) \simeq {\mathcal O}_{C^{\mathrm{reg}}_b}
\end{equation}
where $C^{\mathrm{reg}}_b \subset C_b$ is the regular locus; we note that \cite[Proposition 3.2]{MSY} only handles integral locally planar curves, but the proof of \cite[Proposition 6.3]{MRV2} generalizes all the relevant arguments to reduced ones.

Next, we recall the natural action 
\[
\mu_b: J^{\underline{0}}_{C_b} \times (\overline{J}_{C_b}^{\phi'_b} )^{\times 3} \to (\overline{J}_{C_b}^{\phi'_b} )^{\times 3}, \quad (L, F_1, F_2, F_3)\mapsto (L\otimes F_1, L\otimes F_2, L\otimes F_3).
\]
It is a smooth morphism of relative dimension $g$. Hence we have
\begin{equation}\label{codim1}
\mathrm{codim}_{(\overline{J}_{C_b}^{\phi'_b} )^{\times 3}}\left( Z_b\right) = \mathrm{codim}_{J^{\underline{0}}_{C_b} \times (\overline{J}_{C_b}^{\phi'_b} )^{\times 3}}\left( \mu_b^{-1}(Z_b)\right).
\end{equation}
Let
\[
\sigma_b: \mu_b^{-1}(Z_b) \to (\overline{J}_{C_b}^{\phi'_b} )^{\times 3}
\]
be the composition of the natural inclusion 
$\mu_b^{-1}(Z_b) \hookrightarrow J_{C_b}^{\underline{0}}\times (\overline{J}_{C_b}^{\phi'_b} )^{\times 3}$, and the projection to the second factor; every closed fiber of $\sigma_b$ lies in the irreducible group variety $J^{\underline{0}}_{C_b}$. By the proof of~\cite[Corollary 7.6]{A2}, (\ref{smooth_id}) implies that any closed fiber of $\sigma_b$ has dimension $\leq \delta(b)$, while a fiber over any closed point lying in the Zariski dense open subset
\[
(J_{C_b}^{\phi'_b})^{\times 3} \subset (\overline{J}_{C_b}^{\phi'_b} )^{\times 3}
\]
is $0$-dimensional. In particular, for each $b\in B$ we have
\[
\mathrm{codim}_{J^{\underline{0}}_{C_b} \times (\overline{J}_{C_b}^{\phi'_b} )^{\times 3}}\left( \mu_b^{-1}(Z_b)\right) > g-\delta(b)
\]
which by (\ref{codim1}) further implies 
\[
\mathrm{codim}_{(\overline{J}_{C_b}^{\phi'_b} )^{\times 3}}\left( Z_b\right) > g-\delta(b).
\]
Consequently, we deduce from the $\delta$-regularity of $C\to B$ that there is no irreducible codimension~$g$ component contained in the support of ${\mathcal K}_3$ over $B\setminus B^\circ$. This completes the proof of the proposition.

title: Proof
body_md:
The proof is identical to that in \cite[Section 3.5]{MSY} for integral curves. The $\delta$-regularity is used here in a parallel way as in the proof of Proposition \ref{prop:supp}. Indeed, instead of ${\mathcal K}_3$, we consider another sequence of objects
\[
\widetilde{{\mathcal K}}(N): = {\mathcal P}^{-1} \circ (i_*{\mathcal P})^{\otimes N} \in D^b\mathrm{Coh}(\overline{J}^{\phi'}_C \times \overline{J}^{\phi'}_C), \quad N \in {\mathbb{Z}}_{> 0}
\]
where $i: \overline{J}^{\phi'}_C \times_B \overline{J}^{\phi'}_C \hookrightarrow \overline{J}^{\phi'}_C \times \overline{J}^{\phi'}_C$ is the closed embedding. These objects are supported on $\overline{J}^{\phi'}_C \times_B \overline{J}^{\phi'}_C$, and we can deduce the codimension estimate
\[
\mathrm{codim}_{\overline{J}^{\phi'}_C \times_B \overline{J}^{\phi'}_C} \left( \mathrm{Supp}(\widetilde{{\mathcal K}}(N))\right) \geq g
\]
by a similar proof as for Proposition \ref{prop:supp} using $\delta$-regularity. Then an argument via the Adams operations as in \cite[Section 3.5.2]{MSY} yields the desired (FV1). 

The other half (FV2) can be deduced similarly; see \cite[Proposition 2.9]{MSY2}.

label: thm_main_reduced
title: Theorem
body_md:
\label{thm_main_reduced}
    With the notation as above, assume that both morphisms
    \[
    \pi: \overline{J}^\phi_C \to B, \quad \pi': \overline{J}^{\phi'}_C \to B
    \]
    have full support. We have the following.
    \begin{enumerate}
        \item[(i)] The associated graded 
        \[
        {\mathcal H}^\phi := \bigoplus_{k = 0}^{2g} {\mathcal H}^\phi_{(k)}  \in D^b_c(B)
        \]
        is naturally a graded ring object induced by the cup-product on $\pi_*{\mathbb{Q}}_{\overline{J}^\phi_C}$.
        \item[(ii)] There is an isomorphism
        \[
        {\mathcal H}^\phi \simeq {\mathcal H}^{\phi'} \in D^b_c(B)
        \]
        of graded ring objects.
    \end{enumerate}

label: DAB1
title: Proof
body_md:
For (i), we first note that 
\begin{equation}\label{DAB1}
(\overline{J}^\phi_C, B, \overline{J}^{\phi'}_C, {\mathcal P}_{\phi\phi'}, {\mathcal K}_{\phi\phi'})
\end{equation}
is a dualizable abelian fibration; here we add subscripts for the Poincar\'e sheaf ${\mathcal P}$ and the convolution kernel ${\mathcal K}$ to indicate the dependence on the stability conditions. Indeed, as we mentioned before Proposition \ref{FV_reduced}, (a1, a2) of Definition \ref{def:DAB} are satisfied, and (b) is also satisfied by the assumption of the theorem. Therefore, we obtain (i) from Theorem \ref{thm3.4} and Proposition \ref{FV_reduced}.

Now we prove (ii). By setting $\phi = \phi'$ in (\ref{DAB1}), we obtain another dualizable abelian fibration
\begin{equation}\label{DAB2}
(\overline{J}^{\phi'}_C, B, \overline{J}^{\phi'}_C, {\mathcal P}_{\phi'\phi'}, {\mathcal K}_{\phi'\phi'}).
\end{equation}
Proposition \ref{prop:supp} implies that the reduced convolution classes associated with ${\mathcal K}_{\phi\phi'}$ and ${\mathcal K}_{\phi'\phi'}$ respectively coincide; both are given by
\[
[\overline{\Gamma}] \in \mathrm{CH}_{2g+ \dim B}(\overline{J}^{\phi'}_C\times_B \overline{J}^{\phi'}_C\times_B \overline{J}^{\phi'}_C). 
\]
Therefore, we obtain (ii) by applying Theorem \ref{thm:DAF} to (\ref{DAB1}) and (\ref{DAB2}).

For example, an elliptic fibration with reducible fibers is always $\delta$-regular, but it has $0$-dimensional supports.

title: Proof
body_md:
We can use a nonsingular closed point on the reduced locally planar curve $C_0$ to reduce to the case where both $\phi, \phi'$ are nondegenerate stability conditions of degree~$0$ for $C_0$.

Under the assumption of Theorem \ref{thm_main_reduced}, for any closed fiber $C_b$ of the family $C \to B$ there is a multiplicative perverse filtration 
\begin{equation*}    
P_0H^*(\overline{J}^{\phi_b}_{C_b}, {\mathbb{Q}}) \subset P_1 H^*(\overline{J}^{\phi_b}_{C_b}, {\mathbb{Q}}) \subset \cdots \subset P_{2g}H^*(\overline{J}^{\phi_b}_{C_b}, {\mathbb{Q}}) = H^*(\overline{J}^{\phi_b}_{C_b}, {\mathbb{Q}}),
\end{equation*}    
so that the associated graded ${\mathbb{H}}_{C_b}^{\phi_b}$ is a bigraded ${\mathbb{Q}}$-algebra; for two nondegenerate stability conditions $\phi, \phi'$, we further have an isomorphism of bigraded ${\mathbb{Q}}$-algebras:
\[
{\mathbb{H}}^{\phi_b}_{C_b} \simeq {\mathbb{H}}^{\phi'_b}_{C_b}.
\]
Therefore, to prove Theorem \ref{thm0.8}, it suffices to check that for any reduced locally planar curve~$C_0$, there is a $\delta$-regular family $C\to B$ containing $C_0$ as a closed fiber, such that
\begin{enumerate}
    \item[(i)] any nondegenerate stability condition of degree $0$ for $C_0$ can be extended to a nondegenerate stability condition for $C\to B$,
    \item[(ii)] the relative fine compactified Jacobian associated with the nondegenerate stability condition given by (i) is nonsingular, and the morphism to the base has full support.
\end{enumerate}

Indeed, both (i) and (ii) are guaranteed by taking a versal deformation $C\to B$ of $C_0$ as in~\cite[Facts 2.3, 2.4, and Theorem 2.12]{MSV}, and the proof is complete.

title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{lem:divisor}
    We have
    \[RH^2(\overline{J}^{d,\phi}_{g,n},{\mathbb{Q}})=H^2(\overline{J}_{g,n}^{d,\phi},{\mathbb{Q}}).
    \]
    In particular, the group $H^2(\overline{J}_{g,1}^{d,\phi},{\mathbb{Q}})$ is spanned by the classes $\Theta, \kappa_{0,1}$ modulo classes pulled back from $RH^2(\overline{\mathcal{M}}_{g,1},{\mathbb{Q}})$.

title: Proof
body_md:
By \cite{FV}, the Chow group $\mathrm{CH}^1(J_{g,n})$ is spanned by tautological classes. Since $\overline{J}_{g,n}^{d,\phi}$ is nonsingular, the excision sequence implies that $R^1(\overline{J}_{g,n}^{d,\phi}) = \mathrm{CH}^1(\overline{J}_{g,n}^{d,\phi})$. By the Lefschetz $(1,1)$ theorem, it suffices to show that $H^{2,0}(\overline{J}_{g,n}^{d,\phi}) = 0$.
    
    The rational Abel--Jacobi map $\overline{\mathcal{M}}_{g,n+g}\dashrightarrow \overline{J}_{g,n}^{d,\phi}$ with respect to the last $g$ markings admits a resolution $a: \overline{\mathcal{M}}_{g,n+g}'\to\overline{J}_{g,n}^{d,\phi}$ via a birational modification $\overline{\mathcal{M}}_{g,n+g}' \to \overline{\mathcal{M}}_{g,n+g}$ with~$\overline{\mathcal{M}}_{g,n+g}'$ nonsingular. Since $a$ is proper and surjective, the pullback map
    \[
    a^*:H^*(\overline{J}^{d, \phi}_{g,n},{\mathbb{Q}})\to H^*(\overline{\mathcal{M}}_{g,n+g}',{\mathbb{Q}})
    \]
    is injective. As birational transformations do not affect $H^{2, 0}(-)$, the vanishing of~$H^{2, 0}(\overline{J}^{d,\phi}_{g,n})$ follows from the fact that $H^{2,0}(\overline{\mathcal{M}}_{g,n+g}) = 0$ by \cite[Theorem 2.2]{AC}.

label: thm:uniDR
title: Theorem
body_md:
\label{thm:uniDR}
    Let $d \in {\mathbb{Z}}$ be fixed. Let $\mathsf{a}\in{\mathbb{Z}}^n$ and $b\in{\mathbb{Z}}$ with $\sum_i a_i = d + b(2g-2+n)$.
    \begin{enumerate}
        \item[(i)] When $d=0$, the pullback
        \[
        [N]^*\mathsf{uniDR}_g^c(b;\mathsf{a})
        \]
        admits an explicit expression as a polynomial in $N$ of degree $2c$.
        \item[(ii)] The class $\mathsf{uniDR}^c_g(b;\mathsf{a})$ admits an explicit expression as a polynomial in $a_2, \ldots, a_n$, and~$b$ of total degree $2c$. Here the variable $a_1$ does not show up due to the relation between the $a_i$ and $b$.
        \item[(iii)] For $c>g$, we have the vanishing
        \[
        \mathsf{uniDR}^c_g(b;\mathsf{a})=0 \in \mathrm{CH}^c(\mathfrak{Pic}_{g,n,d}).
        \]
    \end{enumerate}

title: Proof
body_md:
Part (i) is from \cite[Proposition 6.4]{BMP}. When $d=0$, (ii) is from \cite{Pixton, Sp}. For general $d \in {\mathbb{Z}}$, we consider the isomorphism given by twisting by the first marking
    \[
    \tau_d : \mathfrak{Pic}_{g,n,d} \xrightarrow{\simeq} \mathfrak{Pic}_{g,n,0}, \quad (C,\{x_i\}, L) \to (C, \{ x_i\}, L(-dx_1)).
    \]
    Then (ii) follows from the functoriality of $\mathsf{uniDR}^c_g(b;\mathsf{a})$ under $\tau_d^*$; see \cite[Section 7.4]{BHPSS}. Part (iii) is from \cite[Theorem 0.8]{BHPSS}.

title: Remark
body_md:
In the formula (\ref{eq:refine}), we only explicitly wrote out the
    main terms of the identity.  Every term of the identity is of the form
    \[
    \mathrm{coefficient} \cdot \Theta^{k} \cup [\Gamma_\delta, \alpha].
    \]
    As we discussed in Section \ref{sec:4.2}, our main application of the universal double ramification cycle relations is to handle the pushforward of monomials of $\Theta$ and $\kappa_{0,1}$ to $\overline{\mathcal{M}}_{g,1}$. After pulling back the relation via (\ref{eq:varphi}) and pushing forward to $\overline{\mathcal{M}}_{g,1}$, many terms vanish for dimension reasons.  Namely, if the stabilization of the graph $\Gamma$ has higher codimension than the pushforward class, then the corresponding term will vanish. In particular, these terms are not relevant for our arguments so we use \emph{other terms} to denote them for notational convenience. This convention is applied throughout Section \ref{sec:4} for all universal double ramification cycle relations.

label: thm:bmp
title: Theorem
body_md:
\label{thm:bmp} 
Let $\pi : \overline{J}_{g,n}^{d,\phi}\to \overline{\mathcal{M}}_{g,n}$ be the universal fine compactified Jacobian associated with a nondegenerate stability condition $\phi$ where the universal line bundle is trivialized along the first marking. Let $l,m, k_2, \cdots, k_n$ be nonnegative integers with
\[
2l + m + \sum_{i=2}^n k_i = 2g.\]
Then we have 
\[
\pi_*\left( \frac{\Theta^l}{l !} \cup \frac{(-\kappa_{0,1})^m}{m!} \cup \prod_{i=2}^n\frac{\xi^{k_i}}{k_i!} \right) = (-1)^{g-l} [\mathsf{DR}^c_g(b;\mathsf{a})]_{b^m a_2^{k_2}\cdots a_n^{k_n}};
\]
in particular, the pushforward is independent of the stability condition $\phi$.

label: eq:dr11
title: Proof
body_md:
We first prove that $[\mathsf{DR}^1_g(b;a_1)]_{b^2}$ is a nonzero class in $H^2(\overline{\mathcal{M}}_{g,1},{\mathbb{Q}})$. Restricting to ${\mathcal M}_{g,1}\subset \overline{\mathcal{M}}_{g,1}$, we have
    \begin{equation*}\label{eq:dr11}
        [\mathsf{DR}^1_g(b;a_1)]_{b^2} = \frac{1}{2}(-\kappa_1 + (2g-1)^2\psi_1).
    \end{equation*}
    Let $p : {\mathcal M}_{g,1} \to {\mathcal M}_g$ be the forgetful map. Then we have 
    \[
    p_*(-\kappa_1 + (2g-1)^2 \psi_1) = 8g(g-1)^2 \cdot [{\mathcal M}_{g}] \neq 0 \in H^0({\mathcal M}_g ,{\mathbb{Q}}).
    \]
Therefore, we deduce from Theorem \ref{thm:bmp} that
    \begin{equation} \label{eq:dr1}
        \pi_{1*}\big( \Theta^{g-1} \cup \kappa_{0,1}^2 \big) = \pi_{2*}( \Theta^{g-1} \cup \kappa_{0,1}^2 )  \neq 0.
    \end{equation}
    
     
     On the other hand, by \eqref{eq:int} combined with \eqref{ThetaKappa}, we obtain that
    \[
    c \cdot \pi_{1*}(\Theta^{g-1} \cup \kappa_{0,1}^2) = \pi_{2*}( (a\Theta + b\kappa_{0,1} + \beta)^{g-1} \cup (t \kappa_{0,1} + \beta')^2) = a^{g-1} t^2 \cdot  \pi_{2*}(\Theta^{g-1}\cup \kappa_{0,1}^2),
    \]
    from which we deduce
    \[
    a^g = c  = a^{g-1}t^2.
    \]
Here we applied Lemma \ref{lem:a} and \eqref{eq:dr1}. The desired identity is concluded.

title: Proof
body_md:
We first prove that 
\begin{equation}\label{eq:kappa1}
        \pi_{1*}(\Theta^g\cup \kappa_{0,1}) = {\pi_{2*}}( \Theta^g\cup \kappa_{0,1} ) = 0.

 We pull back the relation (\ref{eq:rel2}) to $\overline{J}_{g,1}^{0,\phi_i}$ and then push it forward to $\overline{\mathcal{M}}_{g,1}$. The left-hand side calculates (\ref{eq:kappa1}). Now we consider the right-hand side:  The first term does not contribute since the stability condition forces $d = d' = 0$. By dimension considerations, the only potentially contributing term from the second term is when $g_1 = 0$; however, this term also vanishes because its coefficient is a multiple of $g_1$. Therefore, \eqref{eq:kappa1} is concluded.
    
    By (\ref{eq:int}), we obtain

title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{lem:lowg}
    Let $\jmath :\overline{J}^{-m,\widetilde{\phi}}_{\widetilde{\Gamma}_\delta}\to \overline{J}_{g,1}^{0,\phi}$ be the morphism in \eqref{eq:stratum}. 
    \begin{enumerate}
        \item[(i)] For $l\ge 1$, we have
        \[
        \Theta^l \cup [\Gamma_\delta] = \jmath_*\left(\sum_{v\in V(\widetilde{\Gamma})} \Theta[v] -\frac{1}{2}\sum_{k=1}^m (\xi_{2k}+\xi_{2k+1}) \right)^l.

        \item[(ii)] For $l \ge 1$, we have
        \[
        \kappa_{0,1}^l \cup [\Gamma_\delta] = \jmath_*\left(\sum_{v \in V(\widetilde{\Gamma})} \kappa_{0,1}[v]\right)^l.

        \item[(iii)] Let $e=(h,h')$ be an edge of $\Gamma$ connecting a stable vertex and an unstable vertex associated to $k$-th subdivided edge $e_k$, where $h'$ be the half-edge attached to the unstable vertex. Then we have
        \[
        [\Gamma_\delta,\psi_{h'}] = \jmath_*(\xi_{2k}-\xi_{2k+1}).

title: Proof
body_md:
The genus $g$ universal quasistable curve over $\overline{J}^{-m,\widetilde{\phi}}_{\widetilde{\Gamma}_\delta}$ induces a morphism
    \[
    \varphi : \overline{J}^{-m,\widetilde{\phi}}_{\widetilde{\Gamma}_\delta} \to \prod_{w \in V(\Gamma)} \mathfrak{Pic}_{g(w),n(w),\delta(w)}.
    \]
    For each $w\in V(\Gamma)$, we have the natural projection
    \[
    p_w :\prod_{w\in V(\Gamma)}\mathfrak{Pic}_{g(w),n(w),\delta(w)}\to \mathfrak{Pic}_{g(w),n(w),\delta(w)}.
    \]
   
    
    Consider the following relation in $\mathrm{CH}^*(\mathfrak{Pic}_{g,n,d})$:
    \[
    \Theta \cup [\Gamma_\delta] = \sum_{w \in V(\Gamma)} [\Gamma_\delta,\varphi^*p_w^*\Theta]. 
    \]
    When $w \in V(\Gamma)$ is a stable vertex, then $\varphi^*p_w^* \Theta = \Theta[w]$.
    Therefore, it is enough to consider the case when $w$ is an unstable vertex of $\Gamma$. When $w$ is an unstable vertex, the degree at $w$ should be $1$ by the stability condition. The relation $\mathsf{uniDR}^1_0(0;a+1,-a)=0$ on $\mathfrak{Pic}_{0,2,1}$ yields
    \[
    \Theta + \frac{1}{2}(\xi_1+\xi_2) + \text{(other terms)} = 0.
    \]
    After pulling back this relation along $p_w\circ \varphi$, the \emph{other terms} do not contribute due to the stability conditions. Therefore, the result holds for $m=1$. The general case of (i) follows by a similar argument.

   The argument for (ii) is parallel. It suffices to consider $\kappa_{0,1}[w]$ with $w$ an unstable vertex of $\Gamma$, and then it follows from the relation $\mathsf{uniDR}^1_0(b;a, -a) = 0$ on $\mathfrak{Pic}_{0,2,1}$.

   Part (iii) follows from the relation $\mathsf{uniDR}^1_0(a+1,-a)=0$ on $\mathfrak{Pic}_{0,2,-1}$; see \cite[(34)]{BMP}.

\label{lem:phi}
    Let $\phi(z)$ be the nondegenerate semismall stability condition as above. Then the value of $\phi(z)$ on the graph $\Gamma_{g_1}$ is given by

    \phi(z)(v_{g_1}) = \frac{g_1}{(g-1)} \cdot (z + \epsilon),\quad  \phi(z)(w_{g_1}) = -\frac{g_1}{(g-1)} \cdot (z + \epsilon).    \]

title: Proof
body_md:
Consider the stable graph $\widetilde{\Gamma}$ with $g$ vertices labeled $u_0, u_1, \dots ,u_{g-1}$, where $g(u_0)=0$ and $g(u_1)=\cdots=g(u_{g-1})=1$. For $i=0, \dots, g$, the vertex $u_i$ is connected to $u_{i-1}$ by one edge (with $u_g := u_0$), and the first marking is attached to $u_0$.

   We show that the values $\phi(z)(u_1), \dots, \phi(z)(u_{g-1})$ are all equal. For each $1 \le i \le g-2$, consider the contraction of graphs $\widetilde{\Gamma} \to \widetilde{\Gamma}_i$ in which the vertices $u_k$ for $k \ne i,i+1$ are contracted to $u_0$. The graph $\widetilde{\Gamma}_i$ admits a symmetry interchanging the vertices $u_i$ and $u_{i+1}$. Since $\phi(z)$ is compatible with both contractions and the symmetries of stable graphs, we obtain
    \[
    \phi(z) (u_i) = \phi(z) (u_{i+1}), \quad 1\le i\le g-2.
    \]
    Therefore we have $\phi(z) (u_1) = \cdots = \phi(z) (u_{g-1})$.
    
    On the other hand, there is a contraction $\widetilde{\Gamma} \to \Gamma_0$ contracting the vertices $u_i$ for $1 \le i \le g-1$ to a single vertex. Compatibility of $\phi(z)$ with contractions then yields
    \[
    \phi(z) (u_0) = \phi(z) (v_{g-1}).
    \]
    Since $\phi(z)$ is a stability condition of degree $0$, we have
    \[
    \phi(z)(u_0) + (g-1)\phi(z) (u_1) = 0,
    \]
    and the desired equality follows from the compatibility of $\phi(z)$ with contractions.

title: Proof
body_md:
We multiply $\tfrac{1}{3}\kappa_{0,1}$ on each side of \eqref{eq:rel22}. By \eqref{eq:kappa1} and the projection formula, the first term vanishes:
    \[
    \pi_{*}(\Theta^{g} \cup \kappa_{0,1} \cup \widetilde{\kappa}_1) = \pi_{*}(\Theta^g\cup \kappa_{0,1}) \cup \widetilde{\kappa}_1 = 0. 
    \]

    The third and the fourth terms also do not contribute to the pushforward. To see this, by the vanishing Lemma~\ref{lem:2g1}(ii), we have for any $g_1 \ge 1$ the vanishing
    \[
    \pi_*( \Theta^{g-2} \cup\kappa_{0,1}^2 \cup [\Gamma_{g_1}^+]) = \pi_*( \Theta^{g-2} \cup\kappa_{0,1}^2 \cup [\Gamma_{g_1}^-]) = 0.
    \]
    When $g_1 = 0$, the corresponding term vanishes because the coefficient is a multiple of $g_1$. A similar argument shows that the fourth term also does not contribute to the pushforward.
    
    Thus only the second term contributes to the pushforward. By Lemma~\ref{lem:2g1} and \eqref{no1_stable}, the contribution from the stratum $\Gamma_{g_1}^+$ pushes forward to
    \[
    \frac{-2(2g_1)^3}{48}(\delta_{g_1}(z))^2 \cdot [\Gamma_{g_1}].
    \]
    Since $\pi^*[\Gamma_{g_1}] = [\Gamma_{g_1}^+] + [\Gamma_{g_1}^-]$, the projection formula implies
    \[
    \pi_{*}\left( \frac{\Theta^{g-1}\cup \kappa_{0,1}}{(g-1)!} \cup [\Gamma_{g_1}^-]
    \right) = - 2g_1 \cdot [\Gamma_{g_1}].
    \]
    Therefore, by \eqref{no2_stable}, the contribution from the stratum $\Gamma_{g_1}^-$ is
    \[
    \frac{2(2g_1)^3}{48}((\delta_{g_1}(z) +1)^2)\cdot [\Gamma_{g_1}].
    \]
    Adding the two contributions yields the formula for $a_{g_1}(\phi(z))$.
